page.layout: One column of running text, full measure. Above it: page number 118 at the top left and a heavy decorative running head at the top centre. No margin notes, no footnotes.

main_text.p: tium illud ignotum tibi non fuit, qui prius ædes mihi uendideras. F. At lex uitium sine exceptione pręstari iubet, siue sciēti siue ignoranti emptori uendita res sit. quid enim si oblitus essem, aut ex-tinctam eam seruitutem putassem ? D. An uenditor uitium, quod in re uendenda nō dixit, quamuis id emptor non ignoret, prestare tamen propter Ius ita directò scri-ptum debeat? Qua in controuersia ius aperte cum æquitate pugnat. Vlpianus autem in L. 1, D. de act. empt. re-spondet, uenditorem si, cum sciret deberi seruitutem, ce-la-

page.notes: The running head is a decorative heavy bar at the top centre; its words could not be read. "sciēti" is read from a superscript mark over the e and may be "scienti": the mark is faint. The "ce-la-" at the foot is a word split across the line end with printed hyphens, so the word continues on the next page. Spelling "prestare" and "prestari" is printed with the ligature st and an ę, transcribed as pręstare and pręstari. "Ius" with a capital in mid-sentence is as printed.
